callout.thesis:
The International Space Games kicked off on October 27 at the Skolkovo test site. Teams from Russia, Pakistan, Mexico, and Uzbekistan were the first to embark on a simulated expedition to Mars. Russian and Uzbek students were stationed at the Volga space station, while teams from Mexico and Pakistan were stationed at the Angara space station. Participants will spend 48 hours in isolation, independently solving engineering and technological problems.
The stations are equipped with greenhouses where crews will grow plants using hydroponics and greenhouses. They will also study microorganisms and develop methods for providing food for people in an autonomous settlement. Telemetry systems allow the Mission Control Center at Bauman Moscow State Technical University to remotely monitor temperature, humidity, and pressure. Message exchange between the stations is organized with a delay, simulating communication between Earth and Mars.
The games will run until November 1, after which the experiment will be continued by teams from China, India, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan. The organizers hope to test people's psychological preparedness to work in isolation and cope with adverse conditions. Furthermore, the competition should help develop solutions for the sustainable functioning of settlements on other planets, as well as give rise to new educational and space projects, as well as tech startups.

A launchpad trying to fight insider rugging, prevent dev bundling, and redirect creator fees into buybacks and burns? Yeah, you've got my attention. 

With the #BoycottPumpFun movement gaining traction, the timing could be perfect. And at this early stage, there might be some serious upside if the platform catches on.

Not gonna lie, though. I don't love the irony of a project fighting insider bundling having coordinated buying flagged at its own launch. 😂 Still need more transparency and would love to see a public GitHub.

But I like the mission, the mechanics, and the possibility of getting in early. Worth a speculative gamble. 🎲🤘

Full disclosure: I'm trading more short-to-medium term these days. Selling some or all of my position doesn't necessarily mean I've lost conviction.

Let's see if they can actually build a fairer launchpad.
